model: SHARKY 775 / SCYLAR INT 8 with Modbus RTU communication module
applies_to: Modbus RTU plug-in communication module (Sylop M/N 11024, firmware 1.0) in a Diehl SHARKY 775 compact heat meter or SCYLAR INT 8 calculator.
summary: The SHARKY 775 ultrasonic heat meter and the SCYLAR INT 8 calculator take an extension card that polls the meter over its internal M-Bus link and serves the values as a Modbus RTU slave on RS-485. Every measurement is mirrored in both the input and holding register tables, in ten-register groups holding an integer, a unit factor, the unit as text, a unit code and an IEEE-754 float. This map lists the input-register copies of the float, unit and temperature values plus the module's own settings.

addressing.note: The tables print both the Modbus register (30001/40001 style) and the Modbus address; the address is the register minus 30001 or 40001 (e.g. 40011 -> 10). The worked example reads energy with function 04 starting at address 0x0000. Input register 30001+n and holding register 40001+n hold the same measurement value.

firmware: Module firmware 1.0 (the only version in the change list)

source.title: Modbus RTU Communication Module for SHARKY 775 and SCYLAR INT 8 - User Manual
source.pages: p. 13 (word order note), pp. 16-19 (register tables), p. 20 (unit ID table, example), pp. 22-23 (log 0, error codes)

notes: The module is made by Sylop for Diehl Metering meters. Diehl's own download of this guide (diehl.com/cms/files/..._Userguide_ModbusRTU_EN.pdf) answers 401 without a login, so the link is to the unaltered copy published by the Swedish distributor Armatec.

Word order: the manual says the module sends the most significant register first and most significant byte first, with no byte or word swap. The worked example confirms it: energy Int32 reads 0x0000 0x3039 = 12345 and the float reads 0x4640 0xE400 = 12345.0.

Left out: the Int32 fixed-point copies and their UInt16 unit-factor registers (offsets 0 and 2 of each ten-register group, e.g. 30001 and 30003). The engineering value is the integer times a unit factor read at run time, so it has no fixed scale. The manual recommends these integers for exact billing values; read them together with the factor register if you need full precision.
Only the input-register copies are listed. Each value can also be read with function 03 at the same offset in the 4xxxx table (e.g. energy float 30009 = 40009).
Units of each float follow the unit ID register directly before it (8 = MJ, 9 = GJ, 3 = kWh, 4 = MWh, 20 = m3, 27 = m3/h, 34 = kW, 41 = °C, etc.).
Temperature integers carry one decimal (multiply by 0.1). Error code is printed as hex values and is shown here as decimal enum keys.

Defaults from the configuration table: slave ID 0x0101 (automatic from the last three digits of the meter serial number), update rate 15 s, 9600 baud, 8 data bits, parity 'N', 1 stop bit, log 0 disabled.

registers.name: Error code
registers.description: Highest-priority active error only; 0x0100 means no fresh data from the meter.

values.256: No data update from heat meter (0x0100)
values.8: C-1 basic parameter error in flash or RAM (0x0008)
values.4: E-8 defective primary voltage, running on backup battery (0x0004)
values.80: E-1 temperature out of range -9.9 to 190 °C (0x0050)
values.112: E-7 no meaningful ultrasonic signal, air in path (0x0070)
values.176: E-3 forward and return sensors reversed (0x00B0)
values.16: E-5 communication not possible, update rate too frequent (0x0010)

integration.summary: Wire RS-485 to terminals 90(+)/91(-), power the module with 12-24 V AC/DC on 60/61, then read input registers with function 04 at 9600 8N1. The float block of each group (energy 30009, volume 30019, power 30029, flow 30039) is ready to use; read the unit ID just before it once to know the unit.
integration.enable: No setting is needed in the meter: fit the card in extension slot 1 or 2, connect it with the ribbon cable and power it. Communication settings are holding registers 41001-41008 written with function 06 or 16.
quirks: Floats and 32-bit integers are high word first (ABCD).
The slave ID follows the meter serial number by default (last three digits, with fall-backs for values over 247); write 41001 with high byte 0 to make it static.
The float values are computed by the module and can differ slightly from the meter display; the integer copies are exact.
setup: Defaults: automatic slave ID, 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.
Hold the status button for at least 15 s to restore defaults; the LED blinks to confirm.
Terminate both bus ends; the module is a 1/8 unit-load transceiver.
gotchas: On battery-powered meters keep the update rate above 3 minutes, otherwise the meter shows E-5 and the module reports error 0x0010.
Update rate 0 stops the module reading the meter, so values freeze.
Periodical log 0 registers (30172-30193) are only valid after writing 1 to 41008, and enabling it changes the M-Bus readout the module uses.
